Protocol list must be nonempty, contain only known scrape protocols, and have no case-insensitive duplicates. Default prefers OpenMetricsText1.0.0, OpenMetricsText0.0.1, PrometheusText1.0.0, PrometheusText0.0.4. Native/created timestamp acquisition can prefer PrometheusProto first. 3.1.0 native-histograms mutates global default preference; out-of-order native histogram enablement is effective only with native support and positive out-of-order window.

Per-query lookback<=0 inherits engine lookback; positive value overrides engine lookback for this query. Engine lookback0 defaults to5m. @ and negative offsets are engine option switches enabled in both reference binaries. Per-step statistics requires both engine and per-query opt-in but does not change values.

Global scrape interval0=>1m, timeout0=>min(10s,interval), evaluation interval0=>1m; timeout>interval rejected. Per-scrape zero interval inherits global; timeout0=>min(global timeout,effective interval). Numeric acquisition limit0 inherits global (global0 means no cap); honor_labels=false, honor_timestamps=true, track_timestamps_staleness=false. These change materialized input acquisition, not fixed-input language evaluation.

Annotations are keyed by rendered error text. Duplicate key replaces previous annotation; map iteration has no stable upstream ordering. Warning/info lists are split by severity; limits append omitted-count summary. Preserve captured ordered oracle diagnostics; do not invent a deterministic source order.
Explicit context cancellation produces ErrQueryCanceled; does not become empty success.
Gated function/aggregator/duration/fill/extended syntax is rejected when its context gate is disabled; enabling unrelated gate does not substitute.
Two resulting samples at the same step with identical resulting labels error; delayed stripping does not silently choose one.
Engine validation rejects @ and negative offsets when corresponding engine options are disabled, separately from parser gates.
Invalid smoothing/trend factors, NaN ratio or out-of-range integer aggregation parameter raises evaluation error; q outside [0,1] instead warns with defined numeric result.
Illegal character, invalid UTF8, malformed number/duration/string escape or unclosed delimiter/comment yields lexical diagnostic with source location.
Duplicate matching group on the required one side of arithmetic/comparison errors; set operations explicitly allow many-to-many.
Repeated match without group_left/right or copied grouping labels that fail output uniqueness errors.
Invalid RE2 matcher/replacement pattern or invalid destination/grouping label name produces a named parse/evaluation error rather than silent no-match.
Exceeding query.max-samples returns ErrTooManySamples; no complete truncated vector.
Iterator/select expansion failures remain ErrStorage/wrapped storage error, including associated annotations; no fabricated empty data.
Missing expression/operand/delimiter, trailing tokens or unsupported modifier order yields parse error with source range.
Duplicate @/offset, invalid attachment, nonfinite/out-of-range @ timestamp, or disabled negative offset is rejected.
Deadline expiration produces ErrQueryTimeout; does not become empty success.
Wrong argument count/type, string/matrix binary operands, nonvector aggregation/subquery, scalar comparison without bool, or set scalar operand yields type/arity diagnostic.

absent derivation uses only non-metric-name equality matchers; duplicate equality matchers for a label remove that label from derived output rather than selecting one. Non-selector expressions do not invent argument labels. absent_over_time accepts any observed sample kind as presence.

3.1.0 topk/bottomk/limitk parameters must be convertible to int64 before truncation, then k<1 returns empty and k>input length is capped. limit_ratio NaN is an evaluation error, zero gives empty, values outside [-1,1] clamp with warning; negative ratios select the complement of the corresponding positive threshold. Quantile invalid q warns and yields signed infinity/NaN rather than parameter error.

Sort classic boundaries, coalesce duplicate boundaries by adding counts, ignore cumulative differences only when fact/quantile-tolerance equality holds, and force larger decreases up to previous cumulative value. Missing +Inf terminal, fewer than two buckets, or zero total gives NaN. For q<0/>1 return -/+Inf, q=NaN gives NaN. Rank=q*total; interpolate linearly between finite neighboring bounds, lower bound defaults 0 when first upper>0. First nonpositive bucket returns its upper bound; quantile in terminal +Inf returns previous upper. Monotonic repair is info, malformed le is warning.

Float sums use compensated accumulation, not arbitrary reordering. Means use compensated sum/count until overflow and then incremental mean updates; opposite infinities/NaN propagate through arithmetic. Population variance divides by N, not N-1. Irregular spacing does not change weights.

3.1.0 rejects custom bound differences in add/sub/rate/aggregation, omitting affected output with incompatible-custom-buckets warning. Custom bound differences count as resets. Exponential inputs reconcile to the coarser schema and larger compatible zero threshold. Exponential/custom mixtures cannot be combined.

Explicit reset hint wins true and not-reset hint wins false. Otherwise detect decreased total count, incompatible schema-kind, increased resolution, decreased zero threshold, a larger zero threshold that cuts a populated previous bucket, reduced adjusted zero count, disappeared populated bucket or any decreased comparable bucket. Gauge flavor alone is not an equality change.

Scaling multiplies bucket populations, count, sum and zero count. Negative scaling/division marks gauge. Divide by zero constructs histogram with no ordinary buckets and zero population/count/sum becoming +/-Inf or NaN according to original numerator. Histogram values are not converted into ordinary float samples.

3.1.0 uses signed geometric midpoint sqrt(lower*upper) for every non-zero-crossing bucket, including custom buckets. Zero-crossing exponential bucket representative is 0. Mean=sum/count; compensated sum of bucketCount*(representative-mean)^2 divided by count gives variance; stddev applies sqrt. Zero count and infinite bucket representatives retain IEEE NaN/Inf outcomes.

info identifies series by job/instance, defaults info metric to target_info, preserves base values/sample kind and existing base labels, and copies eligible extra info labels. If multiple info series for the same info metric and identifying labels overlap, newer ORIGINAL sample timestamp wins; equal timestamps error. Info samples must be floats. Conflicting copied labels across info metric names error. If no applicable info labels match, keep base only if all data matchers match empty. 3.1.0 decides absence from copied-label set and indexes base matching by original matrix position.
boundary_domain: matched info with no extra labels

obligations.semantic_rule: Instant selector selects last sample <=target, but a prior sample at or before target-lookback is excluded: the lookback lower boundary is OPEN. A stale float or histogram Sum stale marker excludes the series and does not search through that marker.

For one-to-one matching, on retains only matching labels, ignoring removes ignored labels. For grouped matching, base labels come from many side and include labels from one side; missing/empty included label deletes it. Arithmetic removes metric name even if on(__name__) lists it. Duplicate result label sets are errors.

Empty histogram or NaN bounds yields NaN; lower>=upper returns 0. Compute cumulative rank at each bound using linear interpolation in zero/custom buckets or log2 interpolation in exponential buckets; divide upper-minus-lower rank by total count. Clamp bound ranks to observed total; +/-Inf naturally bound all buckets. NaN observations count toward histogram total but not finite bucket rank.

Empty histogram or NaN q yields NaN; out-of-range q yields signed infinity. Select bucket by rank; traverse forward for NaN sum or q<0.5 and backward otherwise. Clamp accumulated count to total. Interpolate custom/zero buckets linearly; nonzero exponential buckets uniformly in log2(abs(value)), respecting negative direction. Zero bucket extends only toward zero if all observations lie on one sign. Custom -Inf first bucket uses 0 lower when positive upper, otherwise returns upper; custom +Inf last bucket returns lower.

Number parsing first attempts base-inferred int64 and converts it to binary64; otherwise binary64 parsing applies. Decimal exponent notation and numeric underscores must pass both lexer and conversion. Hex integers are accepted, hex floating-point literals are rejected by the lexer. Inf/NaN are case-insensitive lexical keywords.

Classic cumulative precision correction uses epsilon=1e-12 and STRICT comparison. Equal values are equal. If either operand is zero or abs(a)+abs(b)<2^-1022, compare abs(a-b)<epsilon*2^-1022. Otherwise compare abs(a-b)/min(abs(a)+abs(b),MaxFloat64)<epsilon. Both stale NaNs equal only each other; both ordinary NaNs equal for this tolerance helper, without changing PromQL arithmetic NaN comparisons.

Ordinary quantile over floats sorts NaNs before finite values; for 0<=q<=1 use rank=q*(N-1) and linear interpolation between floor/ceil rank values. q=NaN gives NaN and out-of-range gives signed infinity; zero values gives NaN in the helper but a missing window emits no series.

Require at least two same-kind observations and remove mixed float/hist windows with warning. Difference last-first is counter-corrected by adding the previous value for each decrease. Let observed span S and mean gap A=S/(n-1). Each edge gap >=1.1*A is replaced by A/2; otherwise keep it. Counter float extrapolation toward start is capped at estimated time to zero when first>=0 and corrected difference>0. Multiply difference by (S+leftGap+rightGap)/S; rate additionally divides by requested range seconds.

Use compensated sums of x, y, x*y and x*x with x in seconds relative to intercept time. slope=(sumXY-sumX*sumY/n)/(sumX2-sumX*sumX/n); intercept=sumY/n-slope*sumX/n. Constant finite input returns slope0 and original intercept; constant infinity returns NaN/NaN. deriv needs >=2 floats; predict_linear returns intercept+slope*horizon.

round computes floor(value*(1/nearest)+0.5)/(1/nearest), nearest defaults to 1; nearest zero/Inf/NaN follows that exact binary64 expression. clamp with min>max returns empty; NaN bound yields NaN; native histogram samples are ignored.

query.max-samples bounds simultaneously retained sample units, not output row count alone. Float point costs1; histogram point costs floor((histogram byte Size+8)/16). Peak includes retained subquery input/output and intermediate values. Exceeding limit causes ErrTooManySamples, not truncation. Storage errors propagate as errors; context timeout/cancel remain distinct.
3.1.0: require exactly one VECTOR ELEMENT, then return its F field. A single native histogram has F=0 and therefore converts to scalar0; empty or multiple-element input gives NaN.

Require >=2 floats. Level starts at first float, trend at second-first; each next level uses sf*value+(1-sf)*(previousLevel+updatedTrend), with trend combining tf*(previousLevel-olderLevel)+(1-tf)*priorTrend after initial trend. Factors <=0 or >=1 raise invalid-parameter error. NaN factors pass these comparisons and propagate numerically rather than being explicitly rejected.

Escaped quotes/backslash and a,b,f,n,r,t,v are accepted. Octal byte escapes require 3 digits <=255; hex bytes 2 digits; Unicode uses 4 or 8 hex digits, excluding surrogate range D800-DFFF and values >10FFFF. Quoted newline/EOF is unterminated; raw backtick strings admit newlines without interpreting escapes. Invalid UTF-8 is rejected.

Let A=outerStart-offset-range and d=effective resolution. Initial inner start is d*trunc(A/d), then add d if that result<=A. This is global epoch-multiple alignment with Go truncation toward zero; do not substitute parent-start alignment. 3.1.0 inner end is outer end-offset. @ anchored offsets are recomputed relative to inner start.

Calendar functions default to evaluation time if vector argument omitted; vector values are truncated to integer Unix seconds before UTC conversion. day_of_week is Sunday=0 through Saturday=6; day_of_month 1..31; day_of_year 1..366; month 1..12; hour0..23; minute0..59; days_in_month uses Gregorian leap-year rules. Histograms ignored.

obligations.semantic_rule: Aggregation wraps parenthesized expression arguments; by/without can appear before or after the argument list, not both. Parameterized aggregators require parameter plus vector; other aggregators require one vector.
by retains named labels; without removes named labels and metric name; an empty parenthesized label list is valid.
Exactly the pinned aggregation names; limitk/limit_ratio require experimental-functions independently of ordinary aggregators.
start/end within @ refer to outer range query start/end and are valid without experimental function gates; instant query start=end.
Modifier order is optional bool, optional matching, optional cardinality grouping; 3.13.5 optional fill clauses follow these.
Every binary operator takes two scalar/instant-vector operands according to its overload; precedence and associativity are semantic, not left-to-right textual evaluation.
Empty means filtering comparison; bool is accepted only for comparison operators and requires numeric 0/1 result instead of filtered operand value.

Expression forms are aggregations, binary operations, calls, scalar/duration/string literals, selectors, parenthesized/unary expressions, subqueries and time modifiers; 3.13.5 additionally has duration-expression and extended-range forms.

Named calls resolve the exact pinned registry and apply registry experimental gating; start/end also have function-call grammar in 3.13.5. Reserved duration forms have independent duration-expression reductions.
Arguments are expressions; a trailing comma is rejected, unlike grouping and matcher lists.
Parentheses enclose zero or more comma-separated expression arguments; missing delimiters are syntax errors.
group_left/right follow on/ignoring; optional include-label parentheses copy labels from the one side; on and include label sets cannot overlap. Grouping is invalid for set operators.

Keyword-like tokens may be labels; quoted names unquote to label names and then undergo profile label-name validation. In this pin the model label validator uses legacy label name validation; quoted names do not bypass it.
One or more labels separated by commas; this list is not a list of arbitrary expressions.
Parenthesized grouping labels may be empty or end with one trailing comma; missing separators/closing parenthesis are syntax errors.
Matchers are comma-separated and conjunctive; same-label multiple matchers are allowed and all apply.

A label name or quoted name, a matcher operator and a quoted string value; regex compilation errors are named parse errors; metric-name-only quoted form inside braces is also supported by the pin grammar.
Braces enclose zero or more matchers with optional trailing comma; braces-only selector still needs at least one nonempty matcher unless the info selector exception applies.
Matchers support equality, inequality, full-match regex and full-match negative regex; == is comparison syntax, not label equality syntax.

Only a bare vector selector may acquire a range; an already attached nonzero offset or @ cannot precede the bracket range. Use modifier after brackets. The duration becomes a range vector, not an instant vector.
Group inclusion labels may be omitted or specified in parentheses; omitted and empty lists copy no extra labels.
Keyword spellings are reusable in label-name contexts; parsing a keyword as a label does not enable its operator/modifier behavior.
Metric-position names include allowed identifier and keyword tokens; colon is allowed in unquoted metric names but not ordinary label identifiers.
Numeric conversion first attempts signed 64-bit base-inferred integer then binary64 parsing; invalid/range-overflow conversion is a parse error.
An ordinary number is a scalar seconds value; a duration token becomes seconds numerically. Duration tokens use fixed units, not calendar months.
Offset attaches only to vector/range selectors or subqueries, once; unsigned duration/seconds and unary-negative forms are accepted; 3.13.5 additionally accepts gated arithmetic duration forms.
on/ignoring require a parenthesized possibly empty comma-separated list; on changes matching to only those labels, ignoring removes those labels from matching.
Parentheses preserve operand type and change precedence; empty parentheses alone are invalid.
Leading + preserves and - negates numeric value, including signed zero and infinities.
Both signed and unsigned numeric/duration-valued forms are valid in @ numeric timestamp positions.

The public expression entrypoint requires one expression followed by end of input. Empty expression and trailing tokens are errors. Metric/series-description entrypoints are development parsing utilities, not extra query forms.
@ attaches once to a selector/range/subquery with a signed numeric/duration-valued seconds timestamp or start()/end(); NaN/infinite/out-of-range timestamp is rejected.
Quoted metric/label identifiers unquote through the same string decoder, then validate in their destination name context.
Single/double quoted strings decode escapes; backticks are raw multiline strings; decoded value has string type.

Instant-vector expression followed by bracketed range and colon with optional resolution produces a range vector; colon distinguishes subquery from bare selector range; omitted resolution uses engine evaluation interval.
Unary plus/minus accepts scalar or instant vector only; literals fold sign, while vectors retain type. Negating histogram populations/sum/count makes it a gauge histogram.
Only unary + and - are legal; ! is not a unary operator.

Selector regex and label_replace compile whole-value anchored (?s:pattern) expressions; default dot therefore crosses newline in these callers. Inline flags can locally disable s. Captures use leftmost-first RE2 choice, not POSIX longest-submatch selection. Replacement expands $name/${name}/$number, $$ literal dollar; longest alphanumeric name wins, so $1x differs from ${1}x. Unknown/unmatched groups expand empty. Preserve pinned regex capture indices through Unicode UTF8 matching.

Perl \d, \s, \w and POSIX bracket classes are their pinned ASCII class tables; they do not expand to Unicode category sets. \b and \B use ASCII word membership. With i flag, ASCII class rune sets can gain Unicode simple-fold equivalents such as Kelvin and long-s, but digits do not acquire Unicode17 decimal digits.

The reference uses Grafana regexp v0.0.0-20240518133315-a468a5bfb3bc, NOT the Go go1.23.4 regexp parser and not the owned Go1.27.3 regexp parser. Pin Perl-mode RE2 syntax: alternation/concatenation, greedy/lazy repetition, named/numbered/noncapturing groups, scoped i/m/s/U flags, anchors and ASCII word boundaries. Backreferences, lookaround and possessive quantifiers are rejected. Counted repetition bounds above1000 and excessive nested repeats are parse errors; unlimited * and + are not capped by the counted-repeat syntax limit. New syntax in owned stdlib is not enabled implicitly.

3.1.0 optimized case-insensitive prefix/suffix matcher compares a byte slice of len(pattern literal) using strings.EqualFold, then slices the residual using the same literal byte length. Fold-equivalent runes with different UTF8 encoded lengths can fail this optimized path even though the compiled regex would match. Preserve this reference path distinction; label_replace directly uses compiled regexp, not the FastRegexMatcher optimizer.

FastRegexMatcher optimization normalizes indexed strings using norm.NFKD plus unicode.ToLower. Pin BOTH the x/text module v0.21.0 and its selected Unicode15 table under go1.23.4. x/text v0.42.0 selects tables15.0.0.go under !go1.27, but tables17.0.0.go under go1.27. Recompiling the same dependency with owned Go1.27.3 therefore changes normalization data automatically; exact module version alone is insufficient primitive identity. Optimized lookup must preserve the pinned final matcher behavior and not become Unicode normalization of label identity.

use pinned normalization/final matching, with optimizer context distinctions above

Therefore raw owned Go1.26/1.27 stdlib regex is not a compatible substitute even when unicode.Version happened to agree. Go1.23.4 lacks Cn and LC keys, so these property patterns are errors.

The same pinned fold domain must govern compiled regex, strings.EqualFold optimizations, prefix/suffix scans and rune canonicalization. obligations.semantic_rule: Use the exact hashed go1.23.4 Unicode15 tables, not the version string alone and not Unicode17 tables. C excludes unassigned codepoints; Cn is not an accepted key. Relative to owned Unicode17, both references reject newer script names and retain older category membership. These table differences affect positive/negative character classes, regex acceptance and case-insensitive classes.

Pin UTF8 decode/validation semantics at regex and query-input boundaries: malformed UTF8 in a regex pattern is a compile error; regexp text iteration decodes each malformed byte as RuneError U+FFFD, not Latin1 or byte-wise Unicode characters. PromQL label/query validators may reject malformed encodings before regex execution; keep that layer distinct from the primitive. Own Go1.27.3 has matching utf8.go source bytes to Go1.26.10, but that fact does not prove regexp or Unicode table compatibility.

Float + - * / % ^ and atan2 use IEEE-754 behavior; histograms allow histogram +/- histogram, histogram*scalar both orders and histogram/scalar only with histogram left; negative scaling changes counter flavor to gauge; invalid kind/operator pairs removed with info.

@ accepts finite representable timestamp or start()/end(); it fixes selector/subquery anchor across outer steps; offset shifts anchor backward, negative offset forward; @ and offset order has same meaning; duplicates and invalid attachment are errors.

Float comparison filters lhs or emits 0/1 with bool; scalar/scalar comparison requires bool; histogram equality/inequality only compare two histograms; other histogram comparisons removed with info; bool drops metric name.

Separate lexical, syntax, type/arity, disabled-feature, invalid-regex/label, duplicate-labelset, many-to-many/multiple-match, invalid-parameter, invalid-time, sample-budget, timeout/cancel and storage errors; no error becomes empty successful vector.

Range query evaluates start+n*step while <=end; step must be positive and start<=end; scalar/vector valid range roots; matrix/string range roots rejected; timestamps represented at pinned millisecond precision.

Exponential histograms reconcile to compatible coarser schemas and zero thresholds; incompatible custom/exponential layouts remove with annotations; pin-specific custom-bound reconciliation and counter reset collisions are separate evidence obligations.

Preserve signed zero, infinities and ordinary NaN arithmetic/comparisons; stale bit pattern 0x7ff0000000000002 denotes missingness, not numeric NaN; histogram counts and buckets retain their own exact representation.

Whitespace and comments separate tokens; distinguish decimal/hexadecimal/Inf/NaN numbers, signed unary forms, duration units, quoted/raw strings and escapes, identifiers and quoted UTF-8 names; malformed encodings/escapes/numbers are lexical errors.

Instant selector selects last sample <=target, but a prior sample at or before target-lookback is excluded: the lookback lower boundary is OPEN. A stale float or histogram Sum stale marker excludes the series and does not search through that marker.

Arithmetic and most functions drop metric name; filter comparison normally keeps lhs name except on, group_right keeps rhs name; delayed-name-removal defers stripping until final result and affects collisions/regex selection.

Instant vectors are unordered except explicit ordering functions/operators; range series sorted by labels; sample timestamps ascend; topk/bottomk order within groups is value-based for instant queries; annotation representation has profile-specific dedup/merge behavior and must not be sorted arbitrarily.
Power associates right, then multiplicative/atan2, additive, comparisons, and/unless, or; unary minus binds below power; parentheses override precedence.
Range selector takes timestamps in (target-range,target]; no lookback substitution for ordinary range selectors; stale markers excluded; source sample timestamps retained internally.

Matchers are conjunctive; absent label equals empty string; regexes are fully anchored RE2 and match newlines; bare matcher selector requires at least one matcher that cannot match empty; metric name is __name__ matching.

Protocol list must be nonempty, contain only known scrape protocols, and have no case-insensitive duplicates. Default prefers OpenMetricsText1.0.0, OpenMetricsText0.0.1, PrometheusText1.0.0, PrometheusText0.0.4. Native/created timestamp acquisition can prefer PrometheusProto first. 3.13.5 native-histograms/ooo-native-histograms switches are accepted no-ops; scrape_native_histograms defaults false; scrape effective native=true prefers Proto when neither local nor global protocol override exists. UTF8 validation default with allow-utf-8 escaping; allow-utf-8 requires UTF8 validation; other escaping modes are underscores/dots/values.

Per-query lookback<=0 inherits engine lookback; positive value overrides engine lookback for this query. Engine lookback0 defaults to5m. @ and negative offsets are engine option switches enabled in both reference binaries. Per-step statistics requires both engine and per-query opt-in but does not change values.

Global scrape interval0=>1m, timeout0=>min(10s,interval), evaluation interval0=>1m; timeout>interval rejected. Per-scrape zero interval inherits global; timeout0=>min(global timeout,effective interval). Numeric acquisition limit0 inherits global (global0 means no cap); honor_labels=false, honor_timestamps=true, track_timestamps_staleness=false. These change materialized input acquisition, not fixed-input language evaluation.

Annotations are keyed by rendered error text. Duplicate key invokes specialized Merge when implemented, otherwise keeps one annotation; map iteration has no stable upstream ordering. Warning/info lists are split by severity; limits append omitted-count summary. Preserve captured ordered oracle diagnostics; do not invent a deterministic source order.

Explicit context cancellation produces ErrQueryCanceled; does not become empty success.
Gated function/aggregator/duration/fill/extended syntax is rejected when its context gate is disabled; enabling unrelated gate does not substitute.
Two resulting samples at the same step with identical resulting labels error; delayed stripping does not silently choose one.
Engine validation rejects @ and negative offsets when corresponding engine options are disabled, separately from parser gates.
Invalid smoothing/trend factors, NaN ratio or out-of-range integer aggregation parameter raises evaluation error; q outside [0,1] instead warns with defined numeric result.
Illegal character, invalid UTF8, malformed number/duration/string escape or unclosed delimiter/comment yields lexical diagnostic with source location.
Duplicate matching group on the required one side of arithmetic/comparison errors; set operations explicitly allow many-to-many.
Repeated match without group_left/right or copied grouping labels that fail output uniqueness errors.
Invalid RE2 matcher/replacement pattern or invalid destination/grouping label name produces a named parse/evaluation error rather than silent no-match.
Exceeding query.max-samples returns ErrTooManySamples; no complete truncated vector.
Iterator/select expansion failures remain ErrStorage/wrapped storage error, including associated annotations; no fabricated empty data.
Missing expression/operand/delimiter, trailing tokens or unsupported modifier order yields parse error with source range.
Duplicate @/offset, invalid attachment, nonfinite/out-of-range @ timestamp, or disabled negative offset is rejected.
Deadline expiration produces ErrQueryTimeout; does not become empty success.
Wrong argument count/type, string/matrix binary operands, nonvector aggregation/subquery, scalar comparison without bool, or set scalar operand yields type/arity diagnostic.

absent derivation uses only non-metric-name equality matchers; duplicate equality matchers for a label remove that label from derived output rather than selecting one. Non-selector expressions do not invent argument labels. absent_over_time accepts any observed sample kind as presence.

3.13.5 aggregation parameters are evaluated at EACH query step, not only once. topk/bottomk/limitk return empty early if all parameters<1; otherwise NaN, <=minInt64 or >=maxInt64 cause an error before per-step truncation. limit_ratio NaN is an evaluation error, zero gives empty, values outside [-1,1] clamp with warning; negative ratios select the complement of the corresponding positive threshold. Quantile invalid q warns and yields signed infinity/NaN rather than parameter error.

Sort classic boundaries, coalesce duplicate boundaries by adding counts, ignore cumulative differences only when fact/quantile-tolerance equality holds, and force larger decreases up to previous cumulative value. Missing +Inf terminal, fewer than two buckets, or zero total gives NaN. For q<0/>1 return -/+Inf, q=NaN gives NaN. Rank=q*total; interpolate linearly between finite neighboring bounds, lower bound defaults 0 when first upper>0. First nonpositive bucket returns its upper bound; quantile in terminal +Inf returns previous upper. Monotonic repair is info, malformed le is warning.

After delayed metadata stripping, 3.13.5 matrices with identical labels merge samples with nonoverlapping timestamps. Duplicate float timestamps or duplicate histogram timestamps still error. Instant vectors with colliding labels error. 3.1.0 instead rejects duplicate matrix labelsets even when timestamps do not overlap.

Evaluate duration arithmetic in binary64 seconds; step() uses query step and range() outer query end-start. Division/modulo by zero errors. Reject NaN/Inf result, range/resolution <=0, and magnitude beyond +/-2^63/1e9 seconds. Offset alone permits zero/negative. Computed expression duration converts by truncating seconds*1000 to integer milliseconds; literal range/step/offset parsing rounds seconds to nanoseconds first. Engine selection later uses millisecond duration conversion.

Anchored retains last sample at/before left boundary and the ordinary right boundary samples; smoothed additionally obtains sample at/after right boundary and linearly interpolates boundary values (native histograms interpolate bucket/count/sum with layout reconciliation). No sample after left boundary =>absent; smoothed entirely future-of-right samples=>absent. Compute right-left plus interior reset correction for counters, then divide by requested range seconds for rate. No ordinary 1.1-gap extrapolation is applied. changes/resets anchored merge float/native chronological samples beginning at latest sample <=left; need at least one sample after left.

Standalone matrix selector with anchored/smoothed extends by lookback and then trims to relevant endpoints, but rejects histogram-bearing matrices in this root matrix-selector path. Supported rate/increase/delta call paths separately implement extended histogram interpolation; do not collapse these contexts.

Fill substitutes only ABSENT matched side with a FLOAT, never present NaN or histogram. For missing right, synthetic labels are present left MatchLabels(on/ignoring); missing left analogously uses present right. group_right swaps operand sides internally but preserves original operator orientation. All ordinary resultMetric, bool and cardinality checks still run; unsupported sample-kind operations remain removed with annotations. Both empty vectors yield empty result even fill(0).

Float sums use compensated accumulation, not arbitrary reordering. Means use compensated sum/count until overflow and then incremental mean updates; opposite infinities/NaN propagate through arithmetic. Population variance divides by N, not N-1. Irregular spacing does not change weights.

3.13.5 reconciles custom bounds by intersection and sums component populations into common buckets, emitting mismatched-custom-buckets info. Reset detection compares rollup counts between common boundaries rather than declaring any bound difference a reset. Reset/not-reset collision yields unknown hint and warning for arithmetic/aggregation. Exponential inputs reconcile to the coarser schema and larger compatible zero threshold. Exponential/custom mixtures cannot be combined.

3.13.5 applies start-edge zero-crossing extrapolation cap to histogram counter COUNT as well as float value when corrected histogram count>0 and initial count>=0. If the second histogram is an explicit or start-timestamp reset, disregard first histogram layout by treating its baseline as empty with second layout.
boundary_domain: second reset with incompatible first schema

obligations.semantic_rule: Explicit reset hint wins true and not-reset hint wins false. Otherwise detect decreased total count, incompatible schema-kind, increased resolution, decreased zero threshold, a larger zero threshold that cuts a populated previous bucket, reduced adjusted zero count, disappeared populated bucket or any decreased comparable bucket. Gauge flavor alone is not an equality change.

Scaling multiplies bucket populations, count, sum and zero count. Negative scaling/division marks gauge. Divide by zero constructs histogram with no ordinary buckets and zero population/count/sum becoming +/-Inf or NaN according to original numerator. Histogram values are not converted into ordinary float samples.

3.13.5 uses arithmetic midpoint for custom buckets; exponential nonzero buckets use signed geometric midpoint. Zero-crossing exponential bucket representative is 0. Mean=sum/count; compensated sum of bucketCount*(representative-mean)^2 divided by count gives variance; stddev applies sqrt. Zero count and infinite bucket representatives retain IEEE NaN/Inf outcomes.

info identifies series by job/instance, defaults info metric to target_info, preserves base values/sample kind and existing base labels, and copies eligible extra info labels. If multiple info series for the same info metric and identifying labels overlap, newer ORIGINAL sample timestamp wins; equal timestamps error. Info samples must be floats. Conflicting copied labels across info metric names error. If no applicable info labels match, keep base only if all data matchers match empty. 3.13.5 decides absence by presence of a matched info metric, preserving an otherwise matching base even when no new label was copied, and matches base by label hash. Negative-only __name__ info matchers implicitly add .+_info; no name matcher defaults target_info; positive equality/regex name matcher is used as supplied.
boundary_domain: matched info with no extra labels

obligations.semantic_rule: irate/idelta select latest two samples globally across float/histogram kinds. Mixed last-pair kinds remove with warning; two histograms subtract unless irate detects counter reset, then use last histogram as increase; output histogram is gauge. idelta annotates counter flavor and irate gauge flavor. Equal timestamps or <2 total samples emit nothing.

Instant selector selects last sample <=target, but a prior sample at or before target-lookback is excluded: the lookback lower boundary is OPEN. A stale float or histogram Sum stale marker excludes the series and does not search through that marker.

For one-to-one matching, on retains only matching labels, ignoring removes ignored labels. For grouped matching, base labels come from many side and include labels from one side; missing/empty included label deletes it. Arithmetic removes metric name even if on(__name__) lists it. Duplicate result label sets are errors.

3.13.5 float-only mad/quantile/min/max/stddev/stdvar/deriv/predict_linear/double_exponential_smoothing window functions emit HistogramIgnoredInMixedRangeInfo when ignoring native observations from a window that has relevant float observations. Float-count requirements still apply; histogram-only windows produce no float result. ts_of_min/max share the comparator mixed-range info; ts_of_first/last do not ignore histograms. 3.1.0 ignores histograms silently on these float-only paths.

Empty histogram or NaN bounds yields NaN; lower>=upper returns 0. Compute cumulative rank at each bound using linear interpolation in zero/custom buckets or log2 interpolation in exponential buckets; divide upper-minus-lower rank by total count. Clamp bound ranks to observed total; +/-Inf naturally bound all buckets. NaN observations count toward histogram total but not finite bucket rank.

Empty histogram or NaN q yields NaN; out-of-range q yields signed infinity. Select bucket by rank; traverse forward for NaN sum or q<0.5 and backward otherwise. Clamp accumulated count to total. Interpolate custom/zero buckets linearly; nonzero exponential buckets uniformly in log2(abs(value)), respecting negative direction. Zero bucket extends only toward zero if all observations lie on one sign. Custom -Inf first bucket uses 0 lower when positive upper, otherwise returns upper; custom +Inf last bucket returns lower.

If NaN observations put native quantile rank beyond real bucket count, 3.13.5 returns NaN with NativeHistogramQuantileNaNResultInfo; if result remains in buckets but count<total, keep result and add NativeHistogramQuantileNaNSkewInfo. HistogramFraction uses real bucket total for clamping ranks but original histogram count as denominator and emits NativeHistogramFractionNaNsInfo.

Number parsing first attempts base-inferred int64 and converts it to binary64; otherwise binary64 parsing applies. Decimal exponent notation and numeric underscores must pass both lexer and conversion. Hex integers are accepted, hex floating-point literals are rejected by the lexer. Inf/NaN are case-insensitive lexical keywords.

Classic cumulative precision correction uses epsilon=1e-12 and STRICT comparison. Equal values are equal. If either operand is zero or abs(a)+abs(b)<2^-1022, compare abs(a-b)<epsilon*2^-1022. Otherwise compare abs(a-b)/min(abs(a)+abs(b),MaxFloat64)<epsilon. Both stale NaNs equal only each other; both ordinary NaNs equal for this tolerance helper, without changing PromQL arithmetic NaN comparisons.

Ordinary quantile over floats sorts NaNs before finite values; for 0<=q<=1 use rank=q*(N-1) and linear interpolation between floor/ceil rank values. q=NaN gives NaN and out-of-range gives signed infinity; zero values gives NaN in the helper but a missing window emits no series.

Require at least two same-kind observations and remove mixed float/hist windows with warning. Difference last-first is counter-corrected by adding the previous value for each decrease. Let observed span S and mean gap A=S/(n-1). Each edge gap >=1.1*A is replaced by A/2; otherwise keep it. Counter float extrapolation toward start is capped at estimated time to zero when first>=0 and corrected difference>0. Multiply difference by (S+leftGap+rightGap)/S; rate additionally divides by requested range seconds.

Use compensated sums of x, y, x*y and x*x with x in seconds relative to intercept time. slope=(sumXY-sumX*sumY/n)/(sumX2-sumX*sumX/n); intercept=sumY/n-slope*sumX/n. Constant finite input returns slope0 and original intercept; constant infinity returns NaN/NaN. deriv needs >=2 floats; predict_linear returns intercept+slope*horizon.

3.13.5 operations that change metric schema remove __name__, __type__, and __unit__ together through IsMetadataLabel, whether or not type-and-unit-labels is enabled; delayed name removal defers this stripping. Trim operators do not change metric schema by this operator classification. first/last_over_time preserve original name unless input already carried DropName.

round computes floor(value*(1/nearest)+0.5)/(1/nearest), nearest defaults to 1; nearest zero/Inf/NaN follows that exact binary64 expression. clamp with min>max returns empty; NaN bound yields NaN; native histogram samples are ignored.

query.max-samples bounds simultaneously retained sample units, not output row count alone. Float point costs1; histogram point costs floor((histogram byte Size+8)/16). Peak includes retained subquery input/output and intermediate values. Exceeding limit causes ErrTooManySamples, not truncation. Storage errors propagate as errors; context timeout/cancel remain distinct.
3.13.5: ignore histogram elements and require exactly one FLOAT element; return that float even with histogram peers, otherwise NaN.

Require >=2 floats. Level starts at first float, trend at second-first; each next level uses sf*value+(1-sf)*(previousLevel+updatedTrend), with trend combining tf*(previousLevel-olderLevel)+(1-tf)*priorTrend after initial trend. Factors <=0 or >=1 raise invalid-parameter error. NaN factors pass these comparisons and propagate numerically rather than being explicitly rejected.

Start timestamp reset predicate: current ST=0 or current ST>current sample time =>false; current ST<previous sample time=>false; current ST>previous sample time=>true; equality with previous sample time=>true only when previous ST is nonzero and <=previous sample time. This predicate augments value/histogram reset detection in rate/increase/irate/resets. No valid ST metadata means baseline behavior; gauge delta/idelta are not counter-corrected.

Escaped quotes/backslash and a,b,f,n,r,t,v are accepted. Octal byte escapes require 3 digits <=255; hex bytes 2 digits; Unicode uses 4 or 8 hex digits, excluding surrogate range D800-DFFF and values >10FFFF. Quoted newline/EOF is unterminated; raw backtick strings admit newlines without interpreting escapes. Invalid UTF-8 is rejected.

Let A=outerStart-offset-range and d=effective resolution. Initial inner start is d*trunc(A/d), then add d if that result<=A. This is global epoch-multiple alignment with Go truncation toward zero; do not substitute parent-start alignment. 3.13.5 inner end is last actually evaluated outer step-offset, not a trailing nonaligned requested end. @ anchored offsets are recomputed relative to inner start.
3.13.5 clears explicit reset/not-reset hints of native histogram samples when materializing subquery series, setting them unknown, because subquery step changes adjacency. Gauge hints remain gauge.

histogram </ bound retains buckets with upper<=bound, drops buckets with lower>=bound, and proportionally retains crossing buckets; >/ does the converse with lower>=bound retained and upper<=bound dropped. Custom crossing fraction is linear; exponential fraction uses log2 magnitudes and reverses negative-bucket direction. Upper trim keeps underCount; lower trim keeps bucketCount-underCount. If populations change, recalculate total count and estimated sum from surviving populations and representatives, then compact; otherwise preserve original totals.

For crossing bucket with lower=-Inf: upper trim returns whole count if bound>=upper; if 0<bound<finite positive upper keep count*bound/upper with midpoint bound/2; if upper<=0 keep whole count with midpoint bound; otherwise keep0. Lower trim returns whole count if bound<=lower, or count*(1-bound/upper) for 0<=bound<finite positive upper with midpoint (bound+upper)/2; otherwise0. For upper=+Inf without lower=-Inf: upper trim keeps0; lower trim keeps whole count if bound>=lower with midpoint bound, otherwise0. Whole-bucket branches outside crossing retain precedence.

Zero bucket trims linearly over [-threshold,+threshold], shortened toward zero when only one sign has nonzero buckets; boundaries retain/drop whole zero bucket and midpoint is arithmetic. Finite custom sum representatives use arithmetic midpoint, exponential use signed geometric midpoint. Infinite endpoint representative: both endpoints infinite=>0; lower=-Inf and upper>0=>upper/2, lower=-Inf and upper<=0=>upper; upper=+Inf=>lower. NaN bound causes all nonzero ordinary buckets to fall through discard, while a populated zero bucket propagates NaN fraction/count/sum. No sample-type coercion occurs.

When type-and-unit-labels is enabled, rate/increase with named float output validates __type__ equal counter or histogram for the non-counter heuristic; otherwise emits PossibleNonCounterLabelInfo. When disabled, heuristic checks suffix _total/_sum/_count/_bucket instead. This is observable diagnostic behavior over identical input and therefore a semantic gate, not acquisition-only.

Calendar functions default to evaluation time if vector argument omitted; vector values are truncated to integer Unix seconds before UTC conversion. day_of_week is Sunday=0 through Saturday=6; day_of_month 1..31; day_of_year 1..366; month 1..12; hour0..23; minute0..59; days_in_month uses Gregorian leap-year rules. Histograms ignored.

obligations.semantic_rule: Aggregation wraps parenthesized expression arguments; by/without can appear before or after the argument list, not both. Parameterized aggregators require parameter plus vector; other aggregators require one vector.
by retains named labels; without removes named labels and metric name; an empty parenthesized label list is valid.
Exactly the pinned aggregation names; limitk/limit_ratio require experimental-functions independently of ordinary aggregators.
anchored attaches to a range vector, under extended-range-selectors, and cannot coexist with smoothed or repeat; allowed functions are rate/increase/delta/resets/changes.
start/end within @ refer to outer range query start/end and are valid without experimental function gates; instant query start=end.
Modifier order is optional bool, optional matching, optional cardinality grouping; 3.13.5 optional fill clauses follow these.
Every binary operator takes two scalar/instant-vector operands according to its overload; precedence and associativity are semantic, not left-to-right textual evaluation.
Empty means filtering comparison; bool is accepted only for comparison operators and requires numeric 0/1 result instead of filtered operand value.

Duration arithmetic supports +,-,*,/,%,^, unary sign, parentheses, step(), range(), min_of(), max_of(). Binary arithmetic/reserved duration forms require promql-duration-expr; zero denominator is an error, not numeric infinity.

Expression forms are aggregations, binary operations, calls, scalar/duration/string literals, selectors, parenthesized/unary expressions, subqueries and time modifiers; 3.13.5 additionally has duration-expression and extended-range forms.

One fill() supplies both missing sides; fill_left()/fill_right() can appear singly or as one of each in either order. Repeating the same clause or combining fill with side-specific clauses has no grammar alternative.
Fill accepts a parenthesized numeric/duration literal, optionally signed; it is not an arbitrary expression or vector. Inf/NaN are numeric values and are distinct from missing series.

Named calls resolve the exact pinned registry and apply registry experimental gating; start/end also have function-call grammar in 3.13.5. Reserved duration forms have independent duration-expression reductions.
Arguments are expressions; a trailing comma is rejected, unlike grouping and matcher lists.
Parentheses enclose zero or more comma-separated expression arguments; missing delimiters are syntax errors.
group_left/right follow on/ignoring; optional include-label parentheses copy labels from the one side; on and include label sets cannot overlap. Grouping is invalid for set operators.
Keyword-like tokens may be labels; quoted names unquote to label names and then undergo profile label-name validation. This pin validates names with UTF8Validation.
One or more labels separated by commas; this list is not a list of arbitrary expressions.
Parenthesized grouping labels may be empty or end with one trailing comma; missing separators/closing parenthesis are syntax errors.
Matchers are comma-separated and conjunctive; same-label multiple matchers are allowed and all apply.

A label name or quoted name, a matcher operator and a quoted string value; regex compilation errors are named parse errors; metric-name-only quoted form inside braces is also supported by the pin grammar.
Braces enclose zero or more matchers with optional trailing comma; braces-only selector still needs at least one nonempty matcher unless the info selector exception applies.
Matchers support equality, inequality, full-match regex and full-match negative regex; == is comparison syntax, not label equality syntax.

Only a bare vector selector may acquire a range; an already attached nonzero offset or @ cannot precede the bracket range. Use modifier after brackets. The duration becomes a range vector, not an instant vector.
Reserved duration minimum/maximum operator names take exactly two duration expressions; they are not variadic.
Group inclusion labels may be omitted or specified in parentheses; omitted and empty lists copy no extra labels.
Keyword spellings are reusable in label-name contexts; parsing a keyword as a label does not enable its operator/modifier behavior.
Metric-position names include allowed identifier and keyword tokens; colon is allowed in unquoted metric names but not ordinary label identifiers.
Numeric conversion first attempts signed 64-bit base-inferred integer then binary64 parsing; invalid/range-overflow conversion is a parse error.
An ordinary number is a scalar seconds value; a duration token becomes seconds numerically. Duration tokens use fixed units, not calendar months.
Offsets may be zero or negative; duration arithmetic and parenthesized forms require duration-expr; literal magnitude is checked against signed duration bounds.
Offset attaches only to vector/range selectors or subqueries, once; unsigned duration/seconds and unary-negative forms are accepted; 3.13.5 additionally accepts gated arithmetic duration forms.
on/ignoring require a parenthesized possibly empty comma-separated list; on changes matching to only those labels, ignoring removes those labels from matching.
Parenthesized duration expressions require duration-expr gate even when wrapping a constant; parentheses preserve explicit grouping.
Parentheses preserve operand type and change precedence; empty parentheses alone are invalid.
Literal ranges/resolutions must be >0 at parse time; computed expressions are checked after query step/range are substituted.
Leading + preserves and - negates numeric value, including signed zero and infinities.
Both signed and unsigned numeric/duration-valued forms are valid in @ numeric timestamp positions.
smoothed attaches to a range vector, under extended-range-selectors, and cannot coexist with anchored or repeat; allowed functions are rate/increase/delta.

The public expression entrypoint requires one expression followed by end of input. Empty expression and trailing tokens are errors. Metric/series-description entrypoints are development parsing utilities, not extra query forms.
@ attaches once to a selector/range/subquery with a signed numeric/duration-valued seconds timestamp or start()/end(); NaN/infinite/out-of-range timestamp is rejected.
Quoted metric/label identifiers unquote through the same string decoder, then validate in their destination name context.
Single/double quoted strings decode escapes; backticks are raw multiline strings; decoded value has string type.

Instant-vector expression followed by bracketed range and colon with optional resolution produces a range vector; colon distinguishes subquery from bare selector range; omitted resolution uses engine evaluation interval.
Unary plus/minus accepts scalar or instant vector only; literals fold sign, while vectors retain type. Negating histogram populations/sum/count makes it a gauge histogram.
Only unary + and - are legal; ! is not a unary operator.
Bare metric name, metric name plus braces, or braces-only matcher selector. Metric name plus explicit __name__ matcher is rejected as duplicate name setting.

Fill modifiers require two instant-vector operands; set operators reject fill; disabled promql-binop-fill-modifiers rejects syntax. Scalar/vector filling is a type error, not ordinary scalar broadcasting.

Absolute value; -0 becomes +0; infinities become +Inf; NaN remains NaN. All operate only on float samples; native histograms are ignored. Preserve pinned Go math binary64 result, not decimal re-rounding.

Inverse cosine in radians; arguments outside [-1,1] and NaN yield NaN; acos(1)=0, acos(-1)=pi. All operate only on float samples; native histograms are ignored. Preserve pinned Go math binary64 result, not decimal re-rounding.

Inverse hyperbolic cosine; x<1 gives NaN; acosh(1)=0 and acosh(+Inf)=+Inf. All operate only on float samples; native histograms are ignored. Preserve pinned Go math binary64 result, not decimal re-rounding.

Inverse sine in radians; outside [-1,1] gives NaN; preserves signed zero. All operate only on float samples; native histograms are ignored. Preserve pinned Go math binary64 result, not decimal re-rounding.

Inverse hyperbolic sine; preserves signed zero/infinities; NaN propagates. All operate only on float samples; native histograms are ignored. Preserve pinned Go math binary64 result, not decimal re-rounding.

The reference uses Grafana regexp v0.0.0-20250905093917-f7b3be9d1853, NOT the Go go1.26.10 regexp parser and not the owned Go1.27.3 regexp parser. Backreferences, lookaround and possessive quantifiers are rejected. Counted repetition bounds above1000 and excessive nested repeats are parse errors; unlimited * and + are not capped by the counted-repeat syntax limit. New syntax in owned stdlib is not enabled implicitly.

case_descriptions.description: Observe: Whitespace and comments separate tokens; distinguish decimal/hexadecimal/Inf/NaN numbers, signed unary forms, duration units, quoted/raw strings and escapes, identifiers and quoted UTF-8 names; malformed encodings/escapes/numbers are lexical errors.
Reject invalid input or distinguish nonapplicability without inventing a numeric sample for lexical
Exercise lexical with ordinary NaN, stale, signed zero, float/native mixtures, empty input, name collisions and gate contexts where applicable.
Observe: Power associates right, then multiplicative/atan2, additive, comparisons, and/unless, or; unary minus binds below power; parentheses override precedence.
Reject invalid input or distinguish nonapplicability without inventing a numeric sample for precedence
Exercise precedence with ordinary NaN, stale, signed zero, float/native mixtures, empty input, name collisions and gate contexts where applicable.

Observe: Matchers are conjunctive; absent label equals empty string; regexes are fully anchored RE2 and match newlines; bare matcher selector requires at least one matcher that cannot match empty; metric name is __name__ matching.
Reject invalid input or distinguish nonapplicability without inventing a numeric sample for selector
Exercise selector with ordinary NaN, stale, signed zero, float/native mixtures, empty input, name collisions and gate contexts where applicable.

Observe: Instant selector selects last sample <=target, but a prior sample at or before target-lookback is excluded: the lookback lower boundary is OPEN. A stale float or histogram Sum stale marker excludes the series and does not search through that marker.
Reject invalid input or distinguish nonapplicability without inventing a numeric sample for lookback
Exercise lookback with ordinary NaN, stale, signed zero, float/native mixtures, empty input, name collisions and gate contexts where applicable.
Observe: Range selector takes timestamps in (target-range,target]; no lookback substitution for ordinary range selectors; stale markers excluded; source sample timestamps retained internally.
Reject invalid input or distinguish nonapplicability without inventing a numeric sample for range-window
Exercise range-window with ordinary NaN, stale, signed zero, float/native mixtures, empty input, name collisions and gate contexts where applicable.

Observe: Evaluate expression on its own globally aligned resolution grid, independent of parent start; omitted resolution uses evaluation interval; range is left-open/right-closed; nested @ and offset retain their own time anchors.
Reject invalid input or distinguish nonapplicability without inventing a numeric sample for subquery
Exercise subquery with ordinary NaN, stale, signed zero, float/native mixtures, empty input, name collisions and gate contexts where applicable.

Observe: @ accepts finite representable timestamp or start()/end(); it fixes selector/subquery anchor across outer steps; offset shifts anchor backward, negative offset forward; @ and offset order has same meaning; duplicates and invalid attachment are errors.
Reject invalid input or distinguish nonapplicability without inventing a numeric sample for at-offset
Exercise at-offset with ordinary NaN, stale, signed zero, float/native mixtures, empty input, name collisions and gate contexts where applicable.

Observe: Range query evaluates start+n*step while <=end; step must be positive and start<=end; scalar/vector valid range roots; matrix/string range roots rejected; timestamps represented at pinned millisecond precision.
Reject invalid input or distinguish nonapplicability without inventing a numeric sample for grid
Exercise grid with ordinary NaN, stale, signed zero, float/native mixtures, empty input, name collisions and gate contexts where applicable.

Observe: Preserve signed zero, infinities and ordinary NaN arithmetic/comparisons; stale bit pattern 0x7ff0000000000002 denotes missingness, not numeric NaN; histogram counts and buckets retain their own exact representation.

case_descriptions.description: Observe: Require at least two same-kind observations and remove mixed float/hist windows with warning. Difference last-first is counter-corrected by adding the previous value for each decrease. Let observed span S and mean gap A=S/(n-1). Each edge gap >=1.1*A is replaced by A/2; otherwise keep it. Counter float extrapolation toward start is capped at estimated time to zero when first>=0 and corrected difference>0. Multiply difference by (S+leftGap+rightGap)/S; rate additionally divides by requested range seconds.

case_descriptions.description: Observe: Sort classic boundaries, coalesce duplicate boundaries by adding counts, ignore cumulative differences only when fact/quantile-tolerance equality holds, and force larger decreases up to previous cumulative value. Missing +Inf terminal, fewer than two buckets, or zero total gives NaN. For q<0/>1 return -/+Inf, q=NaN gives NaN. Rank=q*total; interpolate linearly between finite neighboring bounds, lower bound defaults 0 when first upper>0. First nonpositive bucket returns its upper bound; quantile in terminal +Inf returns previous upper. Monotonic repair is info, malformed le is warning.

Zero bucket extends only toward zero if all observations lie on one sign. Custom -Inf first bucket uses 0 lower when positive upper, otherwise returns upper; custom +Inf last bucket returns lower.

case_descriptions.description: Observe: info identifies series by job/instance, defaults info metric to target_info, preserves base values/sample kind and existing base labels, and copies eligible extra info labels. If multiple info series for the same info metric and identifying labels overlap, newer ORIGINAL sample timestamp wins; equal timestamps error. Info samples must be floats. Conflicting copied labels across info metric names error. If no applicable info labels match, keep base only if all data matchers match empty. 3.13.5 decides absence by presence of a matched info metric, preserving an otherwise matching base even when no new label was copied, and matches base by label hash. Negative-only __name__ info matchers implicitly add .+_info; no name matcher defaults target_info; positive equality/regex name matcher is used as supplied.
case_descriptions.status: authored-required-observation; execution belongs to release coverage

case_descriptions.description: Observe: 3.13.5 reconciles custom bounds by intersection and sums component populations into common buckets, emitting mismatched-custom-buckets info. Exponential/custom mixtures cannot be combined.

case_descriptions.description: Observe: Evaluate duration arithmetic in binary64 seconds; step() uses query step and range() outer query end-start. Division/modulo by zero errors. Reject NaN/Inf result, range/resolution <=0, and magnitude beyond +/-2^63/1e9 seconds. Offset alone permits zero/negative. Computed expression duration converts by truncating seconds*1000 to integer milliseconds; literal range/step/offset parsing rounds seconds to nanoseconds first. Engine selection later uses millisecond duration conversion.

case_descriptions.description: Observe: Anchored retains last sample at/before left boundary and the ordinary right boundary samples; smoothed additionally obtains sample at/after right boundary and linearly interpolates boundary values (native histograms interpolate bucket/count/sum with layout reconciliation). No sample after left boundary =>absent; smoothed entirely future-of-right samples=>absent. Compute right-left plus interior reset correction for counters, then divide by requested range seconds for rate. No ordinary 1.1-gap extrapolation is applied. changes/resets anchored merge float/native chronological samples beginning at latest sample <=left; need at least one sample after left.

case_descriptions.description: Observe: histogram </ bound retains buckets with upper<=bound, drops buckets with lower>=bound, and proportionally retains crossing buckets; >/ does the converse with lower>=bound retained and upper<=bound dropped. Custom crossing fraction is linear; exponential fraction uses log2 magnitudes and reverses negative-bucket direction. Upper trim keeps underCount; lower trim keeps bucketCount-underCount. If populations change, recalculate total count and estimated sum from surviving populations and representatives, then compact; otherwise preserve original totals.

case_descriptions.description: Observe: Zero bucket trims linearly over [-threshold,+threshold], shortened toward zero when only one sign has nonzero buckets; boundaries retain/drop whole zero bucket and midpoint is arithmetic. Finite custom sum representatives use arithmetic midpoint, exponential use signed geometric midpoint. Infinite endpoint representative: both endpoints infinite=>0; lower=-Inf and upper>0=>upper/2, lower=-Inf and upper<=0=>upper; upper=+Inf=>lower. NaN bound causes all nonzero ordinary buckets to fall through discard, while a populated zero bucket propagates NaN fraction/count/sum. No sample-type coercion occurs.

case_descriptions.description: Observe: For crossing bucket with lower=-Inf: upper trim returns whole count if bound>=upper; if 0<bound<finite positive upper keep count*bound/upper with midpoint bound/2; if upper<=0 keep whole count with midpoint bound; otherwise keep0. Lower trim returns whole count if bound<=lower, or count*(1-bound/upper) for 0<=bound<finite positive upper with midpoint (bound+upper)/2; otherwise0. For upper=+Inf without lower=-Inf: upper trim keeps0; lower trim keeps whole count if bound>=lower with midpoint bound, otherwise0. Whole-bucket branches outside crossing retain precedence.

case_descriptions.description: Observe: The reference uses Grafana regexp v0.0.0-20240518133315-a468a5bfb3bc, NOT the Go go1.23.4 regexp parser and not the owned Go1.27.3 regexp parser. Pin Perl-mode RE2 syntax: alternation/concatenation, greedy/lazy repetition, named/numbered/noncapturing groups, scoped i/m/s/U flags, anchors and ASCII word boundaries. Backreferences, lookaround and possessive quantifiers are rejected. Counted repetition bounds above1000 and excessive nested repeats are parse errors; unlimited * and + are not capped by the counted-repeat syntax limit. New syntax in owned stdlib is not enabled implicitly.

Observe: Pinned Grafana syntax unicodeTable accepts exact case-sensitive keys from runtime unicode.Categories and unicode.Scripts, plus special Any. It does NOT consult unicode.Properties or CategoryAliases, normalize case/separators, or recognize Assigned/ASCII aliases. Therefore raw owned Go1.26/1.27 stdlib regex is not a compatible substitute even when unicode.Version happened to agree. Go1.23.4 lacks Cn and LC keys, so these property patterns are errors.

Observe: 3.1.0 optimized case-insensitive prefix/suffix matcher compares a byte slice of len(pattern literal) using strings.EqualFold, then slices the residual using the same literal byte length. Fold-equivalent runes with different UTF8 encoded lengths can fail this optimized path even though the compiled regex would match. Preserve this reference path distinction; label_replace directly uses compiled regexp, not the FastRegexMatcher optimizer.
Reject unsupported property/syntax or retain reference nonmatch instead of silently inheriting owned Go1.27.3 acceptance for matcher-optimization-fold-length
Exercise selector matcher, optimized matcher and label_replace independently; use source-derived probe partitions below without claiming executed goldens.

Observe: FastRegexMatcher optimization normalizes indexed strings using norm.NFKD plus unicode.ToLower. Pin BOTH the x/text module v0.21.0 and its selected Unicode15 table under go1.23.4. x/text v0.42.0 selects tables15.0.0.go under !go1.27, but tables17.0.0.go under go1.27. Recompiling the same dependency with owned Go1.27.3 therefore changes normalization data automatically; exact module version alone is insufficient primitive identity. Optimized lookup must preserve the pinned final matcher behavior and not become Unicode normalization of label identity.

probes.expected: distinct byte strings/labels, not canonically merged

case_descriptions.description: Observe: Selector regex and label_replace compile whole-value anchored (?s:pattern) expressions; default dot therefore crosses newline in these callers. Inline flags can locally disable s. Captures use leftmost-first RE2 choice, not POSIX longest-submatch selection. Replacement expands $name/${name}/$number, $$ literal dollar; longest alphanumeric name wins, so $1x differs from ${1}x. Unknown/unmatched groups expand empty. Preserve pinned regex capture indices through Unicode UTF8 matching.
Reject unsupported property/syntax or retain reference nonmatch instead of silently inheriting owned Go1.27.3 acceptance for anchoring-captures-replacement
Exercise selector matcher, optimized matcher and label_replace independently; use source-derived probe partitions below without claiming executed goldens.

Observe: Pin UTF8 decode/validation semantics at regex and query-input boundaries: malformed UTF8 in a regex pattern is a compile error; regexp text iteration decodes each malformed byte as RuneError U+FFFD, not Latin1 or byte-wise Unicode characters. PromQL label/query validators may reject malformed encodings before regex execution; keep that layer distinct from the primitive. Own Go1.27.3 has matching utf8.go source bytes to Go1.26.10, but that fact does not prove regexp or Unicode table compatibility.

probes.expected: apply earlier UTF8 validation; do not bypass validation because regex primitive can decode RuneError

version_changes.description: 3.13.5 adds duration expression, extended range, binary fill, type/unit diagnostics and start timestamp engine contexts.
native-histograms and ooo-native-histograms switches become no-ops; native scrape configuration controls acquisition in 3.13.5.
3.13.5 annotation categories add histogram mixed-range, sort-in-range, NaN quantile/fraction, reset-collision and custom-bucket-reconciliation observations.
3.13.5 introduces histogram trim operators </ and >/; overload and finite/zero/infinite boundary rules are independently classified.

Grammar/token declarations, every binary feature switch and registration, every function signature and every named annotation are source-classified; private declarations map to responsibility families rather than demanded helper implementations.

Grammar/token declarations, every binary feature switch and registration, every function signature and every named annotation are source-classified; private declarations map to responsibility families rather than demanded helper implementations.
Both pins exclude exact lookback lower boundary; earlier inclusive wording was corrected from vectorSelectorSingle.
3.1.0 irate/idelta ignore histograms and take latest two floats; 3.13.5 takes latest two globally across kinds.
3.1.0 sort retains histogram samples and orders by float field; 3.13.5 filters histogram samples.
3.13.5 ts_of_first/last consider both float and histogram observation timestamps.
3.13.5 histogram custom variance representatives become arithmetic midpoints, unlike 3.1.0 geometric custom midpoint behavior.
3.13.5 native counter extrapolation caps start gap using histogram zero-count estimate; subquery histogram explicit reset hints become unknown.
go1.23.4 / Unicode15.0.0 / grafana-regexp v0.0.0-20240518133315-a468a5bfb3bc / xtext v0.21.0 selected Unicode15; owned Go1.27.3 / Unicode17 is not equivalent.
go1.26.10 / Unicode15.0.0 / grafana-regexp v0.0.0-20250905093917-f7b3be9d1853 / xtext v0.42.0 selected Unicode15; owned Go1.27.3 / Unicode17 is not equivalent.
Go1.23.4 and Go1.26.10 both report Unicode15.0.0, but newer C includes unassigned codepoints and adds exact Cn/LC category names.
Go1.26/1.27 stdlib regex accepts canonicalized/aliased property names, Assigned and ASCII; both pinned Grafana regex parsers do not.
Unicode17 adds eleven script keys, 10615 formerly unassigned codepoints, new fold pairs and category reassignments. Do not use owned Unicode17 tables for either reference.
Prometheus3.13.5 case-insensitive optimized prefix/suffix scans account for unequal UTF8 fold lengths, unlike3.1.0 fixed-byte slicing.
x/text0.42 selects Unicode17 normalization tables when rebuilt under Go1.27; referenceGo1.26 selects Unicode15 despite same x/text module pin.
